title: Find out about EPR
productTeams:
Registration & enrolment product team;
Approve & Monitor Compliance product team
opportunity:
Producers have complex requirements under EPR legislation for registering, reporting their packaging data and meeting their recycling obligations. Many producers rely on GOV.UK guidance to try to understand these requirements. However, many producers find that GOV.UK guidance fails to give them an adequate understanding of their requirements, is in an unsuitable format for completing EPR tasks;

Producers find GOV.UK guidance too long, too general and jargon-heavy. They often have to have several browser tabs open, or even need to print guidance out, when working on a task. Poor understanding, and under-use, of guidance leads to poor compliance and heavy demand on helpdesks.
desiredBehaviourChange: Organisations understand that EPR may be relevant and know where to go to check what they need to do next

title: Understand eligibility
productTeams:
Registration & enrolment product team;
Approve & Monitor Compliance product team
opportunity: Many businesses do not understand whether they need to register under extended producer responsibility (EPR) for packaging. Businesses have no straightforward way to find out if they need to register. Many rely on GOV.UK guidance but it is complex, often misunderstood, fails to reach all producers who might be obligated under EPR. As a result, some are NOT registering when they should. This creates compliance risks for them,  increases their need for support from contact centres and compliance scheme operators, hampers implementation of EPR policy
desiredBehaviourChange: Feeling confident about in-scope or out-of-scope decision. A business identifies it meets the EPR thresholds and must register

title: Create an account and get "Approved Person" verified
opportunity:
All internal and external users of the ‘Report packaging data’ (RPD) service need to authenticate themselves to get access to different parts of the service.

Defra ID is the strategic authentication solution for all Defra services but it has many known accessibility, technical and usability problems. 

We need to understand how Defra ID would work for RPD and to try to make it extensible to other EPR services.
ideas: Identity and organisation management - Defra ID integration, organisation record, delegation model (common capabilities)
successMeasure: account activated; Approved Person verified; time from account creation to regulator approval; avoidable support contacts about direct-vs-scheme route. Evidence: SPI-006, SPI-007, SPI-011, UN-039, UN-054, UN-095.
desiredBehaviourChange: The right accountable person creates the account and can delegate operational work without losing legal accountability. Evidence: UN-039, UN-054, UN-095; PP-039, PP-054, PP-095.

title: Organisation register and upload details
opportunity:
Businesses that meet financial and packaging thresholds must register every year under extended producer responsibility for packaging. However, registering through the ‘Report packaging data’ (RPD) service is fragmented, heavily dependent on CSV uploads, error-prone, with unclear error-messaging, dependent on opaque fee calculations, poor at showing submission status;

Producers must navigate separate processes to register their organisation details and subsidiaries, submit packaging data and pay fees and charges. They must often resubmit full datasets even when only small changes are required. As a result, it leads to repeated resubmissions, delayed approvals, compliance risk, reduced trust in the service. Overall, the system fails to support accurate first-time submissions and resubmissions within statutory deadlines.
successMeasure: registration application submitted; fee paid; % applications complete without regulator query; time from submission to registration decision. Evidence: SPI-009, SPI-010, SPI-011, UN-040, UN-041, UN-053.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers submit organisation, brand, partner, and registration-fee information correctly first time. Evidence: UN-040, UN-041, UN-053; PP-040, PP-041, PP-053.

title: Collect packaging data, classify data, data formatting
opportunity:
Producers have to submit complex packaging data at least once a year to meet extended producer responsibility requirements. However, many producers have difficulty preparing their data, submitting data using CSVs, understanding validation, and understanding GOV.UK guidance about how to submit. As a result, it leads to avoidable compliance risk for producers, repeated submissions, reduced trust in the service by all users;

The current way of submitting data to the ‘Report packaging data’ (RPD) service, by CSV upload, is manual and time-consuming, error-prone, with poor validation. All users complain about the CSV-uploading process. Most – and certainly the largest – compliance schemes have developed portals to collect data from their members. In a multi-stage process, they have to export this data to CSVs and then upload it to RPD. Some large producers that report to RPD directly also collect data into software that exports a CSV, which they then upload to the service.
ideas: Simplify packaging reporting - provide APIs for data submission; API developer hub
successMeasure: complete 15-column CSV ready for upload; % classification fields complete; % records with RAM/evidence fields complete where required; producer time spent gathering and classifying data. Evidence: SPI-001, SPI-002, SPI-003, UN-055, UN-058, UN-065, UN-076.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers prepare packaging data using the required 15-column structure and classify responsibility, household status, nation of sale, dual-use, and RAM evidence consistently before upload. Evidence: UN-055, UN-056, UN-058, UN-062, UN-064, UN-065, UN-076.

title: Upload and submitting packaging data
ideas: Provide accepted dataset to obligations and PayCal; Setup of submission routes; Support submission configurations; Consume validated regulatory dataset
successMeasure: file accepted at point of entry; % validation errors resolved without support escalation; cost/effort per rejected submission; number of resubmission cycles. Evidence: SPI-004, SPI-005, UN-042, UN-048.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers and schemes upload data, understand validation feedback, and correct errors without repeated resubmission cycles. Evidence: UN-042, UN-048; PP-042, PP-048.

title: Managing PRNs/PERNs (Large Producers Only)
productTeams:
Re/Ex product team;
Meet Obligations product team
opportunity:
Producers and compliance scheme operators (CSOs) struggle to calculate and evidence packaging obligations accurately within the packaging waste recycling note (PRN) system. Confusion and  inefficiency follow from complex calculation processes, unclear guidance, limited transparency in the PRN market;

CSOs spend significant time correcting errors and manually intervening in PRN submissions, while producers are uncertain about their obligations and compliance costs. Overall, users lack confidence in the system, face increase administrative burden, risk delay and inaccuracies in regulatory reporting
ideas: Simplify PRN use; Support PRN evidence integrity oversight
successMeasure: % recycling obligation evidenced; Certificate of Compliance submitted; % PRN/PERN evidence verified on audit; evidence records reconciled without manual intervention. Evidence: SPI-031, SPI-033, UN-043, UN-044, UN-070.
desiredBehaviourChange: Large producers and schemes can understand, procure, and evidence PRN/PERN obligations with confidence in the calculation. Evidence: UN-043, UN-044, UN-070; PP-043, PP-044, PP-070.

title: Pay fees (Large Producers Only)
ideas: Calculate disposal/admin fees, generate NoLs, manage scheme billing, record settlement; Provide liability and payment status to regulators
successMeasure: invoice paid; payment completed without avoidable query; % users who can understand fee basis; reduced off-service workarounds for fee calculation and offsetting questions. Evidence: UN-045, UN-047, UN-057, UN-066, UN-071; PP-045, PP-047, PP-057, PP-066, PP-071.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers understand disposal-fee and eco-modulation calculations well enough to pay, forecast, and explain costs internally. Evidence: UN-045, UN-047, UN-057, UN-066, UN-071; PP-045, PP-047, PP-057, PP-066, PP-071.

title: Repeat
productTeams:
Meet Obligations product team;
Approve & Monitor Compliance product team
opportunity:
Extended producer responsibility (EPR) for packaging involves users completing complex compliance tasks. Currently, these tasks are signposted from the ‘Report packaging data’ (RPD) homepage. Packaging producers have difficulty understanding which tasks apply to them, when they need to complete them. Some producers, especially those new to EPR, find guidance from GOV.UK and other organisations of limited help in understanding their compliance tasks;

Regulator teams lack a single, reliable view of each producer obligated under EPR, their compliance activity, regulatory risk across the system. Information about producers, fees and charges, obligations and enforcement action is fragmented across systems and datasets. As a result, regulators must manually gather and reconcile information with a heavy reliance on grey IT to bridge existing service gaps. [Gaps: understanding of the data that downstream regulatory and policy teams need to evaluate scheme performance]
ideas: Compliance timeline (Dashboard concept); Surface compliance indicators in dashboard; Unify regulator view of compliance across EPR; Monitor obligation & payment state
successMeasure: repeat submissions completed on time; avoidable support queries reduced; guidance/support answers match published rules; account contact and delegate details kept current. Evidence: SPI-012, SPI-015, SPI-016, UN-041, UN-046, UN-049, UN-059.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers keep obligations, delegated access, guidance changes, and reporting cycles current after initial submission. Evidence: UN-041, UN-046, UN-049, UN-059; PP-041, PP-046, PP-049, PP-059.

title: [Cross-cutting]
opportunity:
The scope of extended producer responsibility (EPR) is expanding into new policy areas such as batteries and tobacco products. Some businesses already interact with several services across waste and circular economy (W&CE), such as the reprocessors and exporters service (Re/Ex) and ‘Digital waste tracking’ (DWT). 

However, W&CE services are currently delivered across separate systems and portfolios, making it harder for organisations  to manage their W&CE activity in one place. This uncoordinated approach risks a fragmented user experience; duplicate functionality, inconsistent data across services
ideas: Make service extensible - a dashboard that could allow businesses to manage their access to W&CE services, as more of these services go live
